facts.title: Promoter duties — key RERA sections
points: RERA Section 11 sets core promoter duties, including obligations concerning sanctioned plans, essential services, association of allottees and project outgoings.
Section 11(4)(e) concerns enabling formation of an association/society/co-operative society of allottees as applicable.
Read the exact statutory text together with Rajasthan Rules and the project's Agreement for Sale before applying a duty to a disputed fact.
facts.source: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 — India Code; Rajasthan RERA Rules

facts.title: Section 17 — conveyance, documents and common areas
points: RERA Section 17 governs execution of conveyance and handover of title/common areas in favour of the allottee/association/competent authority, subject to applicable local law.
For Max Heights Majestic, the supplied extension certificate specifically refers to the promoter's Section 17 obligations.
A proper RWA handover should separately reconcile legal documents, plans, common assets, contracts, financial balances, IFMS/corpus and pending liabilities.
facts.source: RERA Act, 2016; supplied Rajasthan RERA extension certificate

facts.title: Rajasthan Apartment Ownership framework
points: The Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act provides for an Association of apartment owners for administration of apartments/property and common areas/facilities.
The 2020 Model Bye-Laws require every apartment owners' association to make bye-laws for administration of its affairs.
Governance topics include General Body, Governing Body, meetings, accounts, common expenses and other association functions.
facts.source: Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act; Rajasthan Apartment Owners Model Bye-Laws, 2020

facts.title: Insurance as common expense
points: Under the Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act, association-level property insurance may be required by the bye-laws or by a majority of apartment owners, and insurance premium is included in common expenses.
Individual owners retain the right to separately insure their own apartments.
facts.source: Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act, Section 14

facts.title: Association can bring action
points: The Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act contains an 'Action' provision recognizing litigation/action by the Association in the statutory framework.
Whether a specific dispute should be filed by the Association or individual owners depends on cause of action, relief and forum.
facts.source: Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act, Section 16

facts.title: IFMS transfer under Rajasthan RERA Regulations 2024
points: Rajasthan RERA Regulations 2024 address IFMS collected from allottees.

Regulation 11 provides for transfer of collected IFMS, after stated deductions for expenses/maintenance/other dues, to the RWA or its nominee or the service agency/company entrusted with maintenance and management.
For Max Heights Majestic, the actual amount due requires the project's collection ledger, deductions, bank evidence and handover accounts.
facts.source: Rajasthan RERA Regulations, 2024 — Regulation 11

facts.title: Unsold flats and maintenance — evidence needed
points: The supplied Max Heights Majestic archive reviewed does not itself establish a clear project-specific exemption for Ayaan Buildtech's unsold units.
Do not assume the same maintenance rate/liability without checking Max Heights Majestic's Agreement for Sale, RWA bye-laws, handover terms, ownership list and maintenance ledger.
This topic is flagged as 'project-specific verification required' in the app.
facts.source: Supplied project archive + Rajasthan statutory framework

facts.title: Sinking / capital-equipment fund
points: Routine maintenance, IFMS/security/corpus and a sinking/capital-repair reserve are distinct accounting heads.
For an additional builder demand, verify the contractual clause, calculation, purpose, separate ledger/bank treatment, utilisation and handover/transfer treatment.
The existence of sinking funds in other projects does not by itself prove entitlement to impose a particular charge at Max Heights Majestic.
facts.source: Rajasthan RERA framework; project-specific documents required

facts.title: Jaipur / Rajasthan building bye-laws
points: Rajasthan UDH currently publishes Rajasthan Building Bye-Laws 2025 and earlier 2020 rules; it also retains Jaipur Development Authority (Jaipur Region Building) Bye-Laws 2010 in the old bye-laws archive.
For historical approvals, apply the version legally relevant to the approval/construction date rather than automatically applying the newest rules.
The app therefore keeps current and historical building-law references separately.
facts.source: Rajasthan UDH official Building Bye-Laws pages

facts.title: RWA and common telecom infrastructure
points: A Rajasthan UDH order adding provision 12.4 to the 2020 building bye-laws states that builder/RWA should facilitate common telecom infrastructure on fair, transparent and non-discriminatory terms.

The order says in-building access/CTI should not be treated as a revenue-generation source for builders/RWAs, and charges to telecom service providers should be fair, transparent, non-discriminatory and on residential rates.
facts.source: Rajasthan UDH order on In-Building Solution / CTI (14-12-2022)

facts.title: Imperia Structures Ltd. v. Anil Patni (2020)
points: Supreme Court considered whether RERA displaced consumer-forum remedies.
Finding: consumer remedies remain additional; availability of RERA does not by itself bar a consumer complaint where the complainant otherwise qualifies.
Use: forum/remedy questions in builder-allottee disputes.
facts.source: Supreme Court of India, Civil Appeal 3581-3590 of 2020, judgment 02-11-2020

facts.title: Experion Developers v. Sushma Ashok Shiroor (2022)
points: The dispute concerned failure to deliver an apartment within the contractual time.
The Supreme Court upheld refund with interest for unjustifiable delay in delivery.
Use: delayed-possession/refund principles; exact relief still depends on facts and applicable agreement/statute.
facts.source: Supreme Court judgment dated 07-04-2022

facts.title: Pioneer Urban v. Govindan Raghavan (2019)
points: Supreme Court held that one-sided, unfair and unreasonable standard-form builder terms are not automatically binding merely because the buyer signed the agreement.
The case involved delayed possession and unequal contractual consequences.
Use: scrutiny of heavily one-sided builder-buyer clauses.
facts.source: Supreme Court, Civil Appeal 12238 of 2018, judgment 02-04-2019

facts.title: Ireo Grace Realtech v. Abhishek Khanna (2021)
points: Supreme Court dealt with delayed possession and buyer remedies across multiple appeals concerning the same project.
The decision is useful for distinguishing situations where possession is legally/actually available from cases where refund relief remains justified.
Always read the exact holding for the buyer's tower/project facts before analogizing.
facts.source: Supreme Court, Civil Appeal 5785 of 2019 & connected matters, judgment 11-01-2021

facts.title: DLF Ltd. v. Manmohan Lowe (2013)
points: Apartment owners challenged exclusion of areas from 'common areas and facilities' under Haryana apartment law.
The litigation recognized the importance of apartment owners' undivided interest in common areas under the governing state statute.
Use as comparative case law only: Max Heights Majestic is governed by Rajasthan law, so the statutory text is different.
facts.source: Supreme Court, Civil Appeal 10930 of 2013, judgment 10-12-2013

facts.title: Wg Cdr Arifur Rahman Khan v. DLF Southern Homes (2020)
points: Supreme Court considered compensation for delay in handing over possession in a residential project.
The case is relevant to adequacy of contractual delay compensation and consumer relief.
Use for general delay-compensation principles, not as a project-specific Max Heights Majestic finding.
facts.source: Supreme Court, Civil Appeal 6239 of 2019 & connected matters, decided 24-08-2020

facts.title: Which forum handles what?
points: RERA Authority / Adjudicating Officer: statutory RERA reliefs within their respective jurisdiction.
RERA Appellate Tribunal: appeals under the RERA framework; High Court appeal is governed by the Act's appellate provisions.
Consumer Commission: consumer remedies can coexist with RERA remedies as recognized by Supreme Court precedent.
Civil Court: RERA Section 79 bars civil-court jurisdiction over matters the Authority/AO/Appellate Tribunal is empowered to determine; this does not erase every possible civil cause of action.
High Court/Supreme Court: constitutional/appellate jurisdiction depends on the procedural route and statute involved.
facts.source: RERA Act + Supreme Court case law

facts.title: How answers are sourced
points: Level A: Max Heights Majestic documents supplied from Rajasthan RERA/project records.
Level B: official statutes, Rajasthan RERA/UDH/JDA materials and court judgments.
Level C: third-party public information, clearly labelled and never treated as statutory proof.
Legal answers show a caution where project-specific agreements or current records are still required.
facts.source: App editorial policy

facts.title: General Body — core role
points: The Rajasthan Apartment Owners Model Bye-Laws 2020 define the General Body as including all members of the Society.
The registered/project-specific bye-laws should be checked for notice, quorum, voting, meeting frequency and resolution procedure.
The app treats governing-body powers and General-Body powers separately so an office-bearer decision is not automatically presented as a General-Body decision.
facts.source: Rajasthan Apartment Owners Model Bye-Laws, 2020

facts.title: Who is a member?
points: The 2020 Model Bye-Laws define a member as an apartment owner and state that no person other than an apartment owner in the project is entitled to become a member.
The model text permits an apartment owner to authorize an individual such as a lessee/tenant in writing to represent the owner for specified rights/actions.
Project-specific registered bye-laws must be checked before applying procedural details.
facts.source: Rajasthan Apartment Owners Model Bye-Laws, 2020

facts.title: Existing RWA bye-laws and 2020 rules
points: Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Rules 2020 provided a transition for pre-existing apartment-owner/RWA bye-laws registered under the Societies Registration Act.
The official rules state that such associations were to amend bye-laws in line with the Act/Rules within the specified transition period, failing which the State Model Bye-Laws would apply.
For MHMRWS, its actual registration date and registered/amended bye-laws should be added to the project case file before drawing a project-specific conclusion.
facts.source: Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Rules, 2020

facts.title: Builder after maintenance handover — Supreme Court (2022)
points: In a 2022 Supreme Court judgment involving a builder and apartment purchasers, the Court examined an agreement defining the maintenance agency alternatively as the builder, association of allottees, or another agency.

The Court observed that the wording could not be construed to mean that after maintenance work had been handed to an association, the builder would still remain the maintenance agency entitled to collect maintenance charges.
Relevance to MHM depends on its own agreement, actual handover and maintenance arrangement; this is not automatically a finding against Ayaan Buildtech.
facts.source: Supreme Court judgment dated 11-07-2022, official SCI PDF

facts.title: Case-law relevance test
points: Each case study is separated into facts, legal issue, finding and MHM relevance.
A Supreme Court precedent may state a legal principle, but project-specific contracts and Rajasthan statutes still have to be compared before applying it.
High Court/RERA orders should be checked for later appeal/stay/reversal before being treated as final.
facts.source: App research methodology

facts.title: Evidence hierarchy

Project-specific verification required: law exists, but the Max Heights agreement/bye-law/handover record is needed before a final project conclusion.
Third-party: informational only and not treated as legal proof.

After valid handover, check RWA bye-laws, asset-transfer records, AMC/warranty status and any continuing promoter obligation.
For lifts, fire systems, STP/WTP, DG, pumps, common electricity and structural defects, use the exact statutory/contractual source shown in Evidence Mode.

facts.title: 2017 Form-B — original promoter commitments
points: Form-B is an Affidavit-cum-Declaration by Surender Kumar Gupta, Director of Ayaan Buildtech Private Limited, as promoter of the proposed project.
It declares legal title to the project land and discloses a construction loan of ₹15.00 crore from Karnataka Bank Ltd., sanctioned on 28 September 2015.
It states the promoter's project-completion period as 31 December 2018.
It undertakes that 70% of amounts realised from allottees would be deposited in a separate scheduled-bank account for construction and land cost.
It states withdrawals would be in proportion to project completion and after certification by an engineer, architect and practising chartered accountant.
It undertakes annual account audit within six months after each financial year, timely pending approvals, and compliance with RERA documentation requirements.
The declaration was verified at Delhi on 29 July 2017.
facts.source: Rajasthan RERA Form-B PDF — https://reraapp.rajasthan.gov.in/Content/uploads/8d8e6882-48ff-4d91-ba0c-1de41998062d.pdf

facts.title: Form-F — extension to 31 December 2021 and continuing conditions
points: Rajasthan RERA identifies MAX HEIIGHTS MAJESTIC, Registration No. RAJ/P/2017/150, Group Housing, promoted by Ayaan Buildtech Private Limited.
The stated reason for extension is Force Majeure.
Registration was extended for 12 months from 01 January 2021 through 31 December 2021.
The certificate requires conveyance of the apartment/common areas in favour of the allottee or association of allottees as per RERA Section 17.
It also repeats the 70% separate-account condition under Section 4(2)(l)(D).

If approved building-plan validity had expired or would expire before the extended registration date, the promoter was required to obtain the requisite extension and submit it to the Authority within the certificate's stated period.
The certificate also sets continuing compliance conditions and states possible regulatory action if its conditions are not fulfilled.
facts.source: Rajasthan RERA Form-F PDF — https://reraapp.rajasthan.gov.in/Content/uploads/FormF//f801ac00-d50b-490d-9e9f-7422d1fc148e.pdf
facts.authority: Rajasthan Real Estate Regulatory Authority, Jaipur

facts.title: Can a promoter charge maintenance before CC/OC?
points: RERA does not create a simple rule that every maintenance charge automatically becomes valid merely because a promoter is maintaining the project. Section 11(4)(d) places responsibility on the promoter for essential services on reasonable charges until the association of allottees takes over maintenance.

For a demand raised before CC/OC, the exact answer depends on the registered Agreement for Sale, the nature and start of services, possession/occupancy status, applicable local law and the project-specific approvals. A demand should therefore be checked against those documents rather than treated as automatically valid or invalid solely from the absence/presence of OC.

For Max Heights Majestic, the app should separately show the available project evidence about CC/OC and maintenance start/rate; absence of an indexed certificate is not proof that no certificate exists.
facts.source: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, s.11(4)(d); Rajasthan RERA Rules/Form-G framework
facts.authority: Statutory/general legal framework — Rajasthan RERA official sources
facts.confidence: Official law/general guidance; MHM-specific conclusion requires project documents

facts.title: General promoter-to-RWA handover obligations and process
points: RERA Section 11(4)(e) requires the promoter to enable formation of an association/society/co-operative society of allottees as applicable; Section 11(4)(d) keeps the promoter responsible for essential services on reasonable charges until maintenance is taken over by the association.

RERA Section 17 deals with registered conveyance of the apartment and the undivided proportionate title in common areas to the association/competent authority. Where local law does not provide otherwise, the statutory framework specifies conveyance within three months from issue of the occupancy certificate.

Section 17 also requires the promoter to hand over necessary documents and plans, including common areas, to the association/competent authority; where local law does not provide otherwise, the framework specifies thirty days after obtaining the occupancy certificate.

Operational handover should separately inventory approvals/plans, common areas, plant and equipment, fire/STP/water/electrical systems, keys, warranties/AMCs, vendor contracts, accounts/transferable balances where applicable, pending defects and a signed takeover record.
facts.source: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, ss.11(4)(d),(e) and 17; Rajasthan RERA Rules/Form-G
facts.authority: Statutory/general legal framework — Rajasthan RERA official sources
facts.confidence: Official law/general process; exact MHM handover status requires project-specific evidence

facts.title: Who bears maintenance for unsold apartments in Rajasthan?
points: Section 10(3) of the Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act, 2019 states that the promoter continues to be the member in relation to an apartment not allotted or transferred until it is allotted/transferred.
The same provision makes the promoter responsible for paying the annual maintenance charge or any other charge decided by the Association for such unsold apartment.
For Max Heights Majestic, application to a particular period should still be checked against the project's legal timeline, the Association's status and the applicable documents.
facts.source: Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act, 2019, section 10(3), official Rajasthan Law Department Gazette PDF

facts.title: IFMS / maintenance-security transfer at takeover

Project agreements govern the collection and transfer of IFMS. Rajasthan RERA-hosted agreement formats can expressly provide for transfer of IFMS to the Maintenance Association at takeover of common areas/common facilities.

For Max Heights Majestic, the controlling answer must come from its registered Agreement for Sale/project documents and actual ledger/transfer records; a generic clause from another project should not be presented as MHM-specific proof.

For a promoter demand, check the registered Agreement for Sale, disclosed project documents and applicable law; after Association takeover, check the applicable statute/bye-laws, valid Association decision and accounts.

facts.title: Does delayed/non-handover automatically dissolve an RWA?
points: A builder's delay or failure in project handover does not by itself establish that a registered RWA/society automatically stands dissolved.
The Association's legal status, registration, bye-laws and the applicable Rajasthan registration/apartment-ownership framework must be checked separately from the promoter's handover obligations.

Rajasthan's official society-registration system operates under the Rajasthan Societies Registration Act, 1958; for an apartment-owner association, the Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act, 2019 may also be relevant. Any proposed dissolution should be tested against the actual registration category, bye-laws and statutory procedure rather than inferred from handover status.
facts.source: Rajasthan Government society-registration portal; Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act, 2019; RERA handover framework
facts.confidence: General legal guidance; MHMRWS registration/bye-laws needed for society-specific conclusion
